Bug_Title: Classes should not access their own subclasses during class initialization
Bug_Explanation: The Parent class accesses a static method of its subclass Child during its own class initialization. This creates a dependency on the subclass initialization order, leading to potential initialization cycles and unpredictable behavior. Specifically, Parent.field1 is initialized using Child.method(), which returns a value dependent on Parent.field2. However, due to initialization order, field1 could end up with an unexpected value.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by creating an instance of Parent and calling the showBug method. This leads to the initialization cycle where Parent.field1 is set to an unexpected value because it relies on the Child.method during Parent's class initialization, leading to a failure in the test case.
